title: Chain-level right-shift comparison of sheaf Hom complexes
statement: On a small ringed site (C,J,R), let K be the category of unbounded cochain complexes of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and H:K^op × K → K the sheaf-valued Hom-complex bifunctor [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every integer n there is a natural isomorphism H followed by shift(n) to (identity × shift(n)) followed by H. No K-injectivity, boundedness, or derived-category assumption is required.

source.place: Section 21.34 (Tag 0A8X), definition and differential of the Hom complex; signed specialization of the parent shift calculation

proof.text: In degree k both complexes have product factors Hom(L^p,M^(p+k+n)). Using the product universal properties from homComplex_exists and the shift degree isomorphisms, form mutually inverse degree maps.

Compare the differential after each product projection. On Hom(L,M)[n] the postcomposition coefficient is (-1)^n and the precomposition coefficient is -(-1)^(k+2n)=-(-1)^k. The differential on Hom(L,M[n]) has the same two coefficients. The degree maps and their inverses therefore are chain maps.

The degree identifications commute with precomposition by source chain maps and postcomposition by target chain maps. Thus the component chain isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism of the uncurried bifunctors. The formulas include negative and zero shifts and zero complexes.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_shift_right
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (n : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (
      Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (C := C) (J := J) (R := R)) ⋙
        shiftFunctor _ n ≅
      (𝟭 _).prod (shiftFunctor _ n) ⋙
        Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (C := C) (J := J) (R := R)))
